title: Akshay Kumar and Priyadarshan Made ₹259 Crore. Now They're Coming for Your Netflix Queue.
excerpt: Bhooth Bangla — the ghost story that reunited Bollywood's greatest comedy duo — is finally streaming. Here's why the diaspora should press play.
body:
The last time **Akshay Kumar** and **Priyadarshan** shared a screen credit, the results were *Hera Pheri*, *Garam Masala*, and *Bhool Bhulaiyaa* — a trio of comedies so iconic they're practically national holidays in certain households. When they announced they were reuniting for a haunted-mansion horror-comedy, expectations were stratospheric.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=sL7V1INn6io</youtube>

**Bhooth Bangla** delivered — mostly. The film grossed **₹259 crore worldwide** across an eight-week theatrical run, made Akshay Kumar's second-biggest post-pandemic hit, and proved that the old Priyadarshan formula still has teeth. And now, as of June 12, it's sitting on your **Netflix** homepage, ready for the diaspora audience that's been waiting.

## The Setup

The premise is classic Priyadarshan: a man inherits something absurd and chaos follows. **Arjun Acharya** (Akshay Kumar) comes into possession of a crumbling ancestral palace called Acharya Niwas in the fictional North Indian town of Mangalpur. He decides, as one does, that this is the perfect venue for his sister Meera's wedding. The locals warn him about a curse. He ignores them. Things go predictably, delightfully wrong.

**Tabu** shows up and immediately owns every scene she's in — at this point, the woman could read a grocery list and make it feel like Shakespeare. **Paresh Rawal** brings the panic energy that's become his signature. **Rajpal Yadav** does what Rajpal Yadav does. **Wamiqa Gabbi** and **Mithila Palkar** round out a cast that reads like a Diwali party guest list where everyone's actually fun.

## The Verdict

Here's the thing about Bhooth Bangla: the first half is genuinely, joyfully funny. Priyadarshan's old-school chaos comedy — the misunderstandings, the physical gags, the ensemble bits that stack on top of each other — fires on all cylinders. Bollywood Hungama gave it **3.5 out of 5 stars**, calling it "a fair entertainer that works best for its humour, performances and old-school Priyadarshan-style chaos."

The second half? It wobbles. The backstory that's supposed to explain the haunting feels undercooked, and the climax runs about twenty minutes longer than it needs to. The Times of India (3/5) put it perfectly: "a crisper narrative and a shorter runtime would have made this horror comedy far more effective." India Today was harsher at 2.5/5, citing "outdated humour" and "weak storytelling."

But none of that stopped audiences from showing up. The film earned **₹169 crore nett** in India alone, with footfalls just under one crore — numbers that most Bollywood films this year would donate a kidney for.

## The Business Behind the Bangla

The real story might be the deal structure. Before a single ticket was sold, the producers had recovered **₹105 crore** of the ₹120 crore budget through non-theatrical deals: **₹60 crore from Netflix** for digital rights, ₹25 crore from Zee Cinema for satellite, and ₹10 crore from Zee Music. Every rupee earned at the box office was essentially profit. This is how you build a hit in 2026 Bollywood — the theatrical window is the cherry, not the cake.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

If you grew up watching Hera Pheri on loop and quoting "Aye Baburao" at family functions, Bhooth Bangla is comfort food. It's not reinventing anything. Priyadarshan isn't trying to make *Get Out*. He's making a three-course thali of slapstick, jump scares, and Paresh Rawal screaming at ghosts — and on those terms, it works.

The film is streaming in **Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam** — so whether you're in Houston or Hyderabad, Mississauga or Mangalore, it's accessible and ready for a weekend binge.

Is it Bhool Bhulaiyaa? No. Is it the best thing Akshay Kumar has done in years? Absolutely. And sometimes that's enough.

Grab the popcorn. Leave the lights on. Akshay and Priyadarshan are back in your living room.
